title: sail event: one line of a run's or a queue's event stream
description: One NDJSON line in events.ndjson: the envelope ({ seq, ts, type, runId, key? }) with the event's payload beside it. The type vocabulary is exhaustive. The families the engine and the port adapters emit have closed payloads, and a call-level event requires the key of its call. A ticket or codehost event carries its call's key when a call emitted it, and a workspace event carries none. A watched workflow's queue event stream, .sail-runs/queue/<workflow>/events.ndjson, uses the same envelope without runId or key, with the workflow it belongs to: its watch set changes, polls, items and dispatches, and the runs the watcher adopted or resumed.
$comment: Closed: every type of a run's stream: run:start, run:end, run:suspended, intake:*, stage:*, step:*, input:materialised, prompt:rendered, script:*, output:*, file:*, journal:append, loop:*, all:*, workflow:route, agent:*, harness:*, tool:*, permission:denied, usage:update, budget:* (budget:raised among them), error:*, ticket:*, codehost:* and workspace:*. The queue family follows error:port in the enum, alone may leave out runId, and is closed: watch:*, queue:polled, queue:item_added, queue:dispatched, queue:skipped_leased, queue:dropped, queue:parked, queue:error, run:adopted, run:resumed, queue:requeued, queue:held and queue:released. The root validates the envelope and allows additional properties, which each closed payload then refuses. Each closed payload $refs #/$defs/envelope, so that its unevaluatedProperties counts the envelope's names as its own. A payload's own if/then/else sits inside an allOf: beside the $ref, Ajv drops the envelope's names whenever the if fails.

envelope.description: the envelope's names, which the root validates: a closed payload $refs this so they count as evaluated

callEnvelope.description: the envelope of an event that belongs to a call, which requires the call's key

consumed.description: binding name → where it came from (null for an optional binding left unbound)

errors.description: why the outcome is error: every contract problem found, each with its reason

rosterEntry.description: a stage as sail.run.v1 records it in the roster

runStart.description: the run header's values, emitted once, when a fresh run starts

fromRun.description: the run a seeded run reused calls from

runEnd.description: how this process left the run; a stop reason exactly when it failed or was suspended

runSuspended.description: a run suspended right before its run:end: on its budget (which budget it used up, its limit and what was used), or on the provider's usage limit (the call that hit it, and when it resets if the provider said)

runKeepAwake.description: whether the run's process holds a keep-awake, once per process that drives the run; the run's, so no key

stageStart.description: a try of a call starting: model, permissions and budget for an agent, steps for a multi-step stage

harness.description: the named harness the call ran on, left out for the default

stageEnd.description: a try of a call ending, with the result it wrote; errors exactly when the outcome is error

stepStart.description: a try of one step of a multi-step call starting, under the step's key

harness.description: the named harness the step ran on, left out for the default

stepEnd.description: a try of one step ending, with the result it wrote; errors exactly when the outcome is error

stepQueued.description: a script step waiting for an exclusive slot another run's step holds, naming the holder

loopIteration.description: a pass of a loop starting; feedback names where the previous pass's feedback came from

from.description: a call's output pointer, or workflow

allStart.description: a group starting: its keys in declaration order, and the ones this process starts now

allEnd.description: a group whose every call is journaled: each call's outcome, and this process's wall time for the group

workflowRoute.description: the move a workflow made after a call: the call's key and outcome, and the next call's key, end or fail

fromRun.description: the run a reused call was taken from

ticket.description: the run's ticket, on a reused intake's line only; the title is untrusted text

envKeys.description: the preamble's names, in order, then SAIL_EVENTS

scriptExit.description: how a script that started ended. A null code names the signal that ended it.

outcome.description: what the exit code maps to, when it has a mapping

errorCrash.description: an exception inside sail, and the call it happened in when there was one

errorConsumer.description: a consumer that threw, and the event it threw on

errorPort.description: a port call of a script step's sail port that failed, with the port's own message

ticketState.description: a ticket's state by type, with the provider's own name for it

ticketFetched.description: the ticket that was fetched, by its title and URL, and how many comments, links and attachments it came with

ticketClaimed.description: a claim that took, with the state the provider reports

ticketUpdated.description: the move asked for, and the state the provider reports

ticketRelated.description: a relation of the ticket to another, and the ticket's state afterwards

ticketEdited.description: the fields an edit set on the ticket

codehostChecks.description: the checks the host reports on a pull request's head sha

codehostMerged.description: a merge the host reports, never one merely requested

workspaceLeased.description: a branch lease taken; took names the stale run whose lease it replaced

usage.description: tokens and cost, as sail.result.v1 records them

promptRendered.description: the prompt of a try, rendered and kept as prompt.md: what it printed and what was appended to it

harnessSessionEnd.description: one per session, with all it spent; sessionId is left out only when the harness reported none

result.description: the start of the text the tool returned, when it returned any

permissionDenied.description: a tool call a step's permissions refused: the rule, and the step's permissions under it

usageUpdate.description: cumulative within its session: the last one before the session's end is what it spent

budgetEvent.description: a budget at its threshold or its limit: a step's carries its call's key, and the run's none

budgetRaised.description: a raise of the run's budget, given to sail resume: what it added, at least one of usd and minutes, and the run's budget after it; the run's, so no key

queueEnvelope.description: a queue event's envelope: the run's without runId or key, and the watched workflow it belongs to. A closed queue payload $refs this, so its unevaluatedProperties counts these names as its own

dedupKey.description: ticket:<ticket key>, or pr:<number>@<the head sha's first 7>

watchAdded.description: the watcher with this pid added the workflow to its watch set: the label it polls, how often, and how many of its runs may run at once

watchRemoved.description: the watcher with this pid took the workflow out of its watch set, or stopped

queuePolled.description: one poll of a watched workflow's designated sources: how many it found, and how many of them it queued

queueItemAdded.description: a source queued under its dedup key; the title is the provider's, untrusted text

queueDispatched.description: a run started for the item: its run id, which dispatch of the item it is, and the pid of its process

run.description: the id of the run the dispatch started

queueSkippedLeased.description: a due item left queued because a live run's branch lease holds its branch: it used no slot and counted no attempt

heldBy.description: the run id of the lease's holder

queueDropped.description: an item taken out of the queue, such as one its re-check found no longer designated or in a pick-up state; a later poll may queue it again

queueParked.description: an item that failed its last attempt, or whose run was stopped: kept with the reason, and never retried

queueError.description: a poll that failed: paused when the provider refused the credentials, else retried in retryInMs

runAdopted.description: the watcher took charge of a dispatched item's run, alive as this pid: after a restart, or a resume another process started

run.description: the id of the run adopted

runResumed.description: the watcher started sail resume for a dispatched item's run, as this pid: the run was running with its process gone, or suspended with interrupted or unwatched

run.description: the id of the run resumed

from.description: where the run was: its status, and its stop reason exactly when it was suspended

queueRequeued.description: a parked or failed item put back in the queue by hand, with no attempts

queueHeld.description: a workflow's dispatch held until a time because a run hit the usage limit: nothing starts or resumes until then, and the queue is unchanged

queueReleased.description: a workflow's held dispatch released: its hold has passed
